newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian police prevent protest at Belarus embassy.
newsitem.headline: Russian police prevent protest at Belarus embassy.

text.p: Russian police prevented a demonstration taking place outside the Belarussian embassy in Moscow on Sunday and detained several people trying to protest against media restrictions in Minsk, witnesses said.
Oleg Panfilov, head of the independent Glasnost Defence Foundation which defends journalists' rights, was among those detained but he was released after about 20 minutes, Itar-Tass news agency said.
The witnesses said about 30 people turned up for the protest but it had not been sanctioned by Moscow city authorities. Minor scuffles broke out briefly but no one was hurt.

Hardline President Alexander Lukashenko, who is due to visit Moscow on Wednesday to sign documents on closer integration between Russia and Belarus, has accused foreign media of bias in reporting opposition protests in the former Soviet republic.

Belarus has ordered out a reporter from Russia's commercial television network NTV and journalists were prevented on March 24 from entering the television centre where they usually transmit their reports.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin has expressed concern about the problems facing Russian journalists in Belarus and asked the authorities in Minsk to guarantee media freedoms. He has also advised Russian reporters to ensure they abide by the law.
